questions.question: List the five steps of the design process in order and say in one sentence what happens at each step.
questions.expected_answer: Investigate: find out about the problem, the users and existing solutions. Design: write a design brief with specifications and constraints, sketch ideas and choose the best. Make: build the model safely from a working drawing. Evaluate: test the model against the specifications and judge it honestly. Communicate: present the drawings, model and evaluation so others understand the solution.

questions.question: Explain how to identify the class of any lever, and give one example of each class with its pivot, load and effort named.
questions.expected_answer: Find the pivot, load and effort and ask which one is in the middle. Pivot in the middle: first class, for example a seesaw (pivot at the centre bar, child as load, other child as effort). Load in the middle: second class, for example a wheelbarrow (pivot at the wheel axle, load in the tray, effort at the handles); it always gives a mechanical advantage. Effort in the middle: third class, for example a fishing rod (pivot at the bottom hand, effort at the top hand, load at the tip); it never gives a mechanical advantage but gives speed and reach.

questions.question: Describe the purpose of the Week 1 baseline assessment and explain why honest effort on it is useful even though it does not count towards the term mark.
questions.expected_answer: It shows the teacher what the class remembers from Grade 7 so that Grade 8 lessons start at the right level and gaps are filled before new content. Honest effort gives a true reading: blank answers waste class time on revision that is not needed, while lucky guesses hide real gaps that will cost marks later. Trying to recall the ideas is also strong revision in itself.
